state_summary: Round 11 reports 685 observed records, 2,645 eligible candidates, no pending experiments and no validation/test records. Latest evidence rejects bracketed m177 completion interpolation across loading, supports persistence of short EA-loaded m92 completion, and establishes steep growth in both sampled para and meta aminoesters. Alcohol and carbonyl responses remain heterogeneous. Observed row alignment reveals that the intended m20 1/1, 50 ul baseline was not measured. Overall retrained Row accuracy remains unverified.

important_observations.statement: H22 requires revision: at m177 50/1, completion is 59.88/7.31/81.30 ml across 50/100/150 ul, rejecting bracketed interpolation. The new 100 ul result is 5.27/7.31 ml, an interval only 2.04 ml wide. Its fixed-100 ul sequence measures 5.06/19.18 at 5/1, 5.20/20.70 at 10/1 and 5.27/7.31 at 50/1. At 50 ul, the new 5/1 result is 6.38/14.51. Distinct short-completion inputs do not replicate one another. Reproducible conditional minima and variation omitted from the inputs remain competing hypotheses.

H20 gains support for persistence of short EA completion. Identical m92 1/1, 50 ul, EA 200 ul inputs measure 5.18/12.01 and 5.72/11.70 ml; completion differs by only -0.31 ml. The single PE-loaded counterpart measures 8.02/20.57. Relative to it, the second EA result shifts endpoints by -2.30/-8.87 ml. PE-side repeatability and transfer to other conditions remain unresolved.

Record 66e712388ecd53b9c22c is m148 at 5/1, density 1.069, 150 ul, PE 300 ul, measuring 6.03/9.46 ml. Discard its stored m20 baseline interpretation. Actual m20 at 50 ul measures 15.84/22.69 at 5/1 and 23.78/34.90 at 10/1, rejecting the proposed 5/1 completion shoulder above 10/1. Its measured 1/1 anchor uses 150 ul and measures 7.29/11.82; the fixed-50 ul lower-ratio baseline remains missing.

H13 is strengthened as differentiated alcohol response. Fixed-50 ul m60 rises 12.20/17.43 to 27.63/36.92 to 46.02/68.74 ml across 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1. At 10/1, increasing loading to 100 ul changes endpoints by -6.88/-4.03, widening the interval because onset moves more. Conversely, fixed-100 ul m61 measures 12.34/21.99, 10.27/15.56 and 3.04/17.24 across those ratios: onset decreases substantially, with a sampled completion minimum at 5/1. A shared alcohol correction is unsupported.

H18's proposed low-ratio m194 completion growth is rejected. At fixed 100 ul, endpoints change from 4.35/36.18 at 1/1 to 4.52/28.27 at 2/1: completion decreases by 7.91 ml while onset barely moves. At 2/1, the existing 150 ul result, 4.63/28.18, is close to the new 100 ul result. Persistence across lower loading and a later onset transition remain untested.

H24 now supports steep growth in both sampled para and meta aminoesters. Fixed-100 ul m86 measures 7.13/14.69, 10.81/22.83 and 28.73/57.53 ml across 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1. m88 measures 5.93/17.08, 11.89/21.50 and 27.58/64.40 under its own fixed conditions. Existing ortho-aminoester m89 at 5/1 instead measures 9.25/17.00 at 50 ul and 8.52/16.69 at 150 ul. Different loading solvent, plug, density and intermediate-loading coverage prevent isolated attribution to amino-group position.

H17/H15 retain structural limits of transfer. m165 changes from 5.11/10.04 at 1/1 to 6.22/23.00 at 20/1, with much shallower onset than m164's 13.35/35.72 at 20/1. Fixed-100 ul m26 changes moderately from 6.85/22.50 at 2/1 to 9.58/26.99 at 20/1. Cyclopropyl beta-ketoester m94 grows from 12.33/26.02 at 5/1 to 21.34/45.11 at 10/1, while m78 has a more moderate controlled progression. Carbonyl count or beta-ketoester membership does not establish a shared slope.

H21's m157 question is substantially answered. Diiodobenzene measures 6.31/10.47 at 2/1 and 6.07/11.20 ml at 20/1 under identical loading, a modest -0.23/+0.73 shift. It is now measured chemistry; routine expansion requires a new condition question.

possible_model_blind_spots.statement: Common endpoint offsets or monotone loading interpolation cannot describe the supplied m177 completion values, m61 onset decrease and m60 onset-dominant loading shift. Separate V1/V2 condition responses remain necessary.

Increasing PE/EA lowers EA fraction and generally weakens silica elution; 0/1 is pure EA. Loading solvent can affect adsorption and focusing. Local measured exceptions do not reverse this solvent-strength relationship.

Donor accessibility, amine–silanol interactions, adsorption saturation, solubility, injection-zone spreading and keto–enol equilibria could contribute. None was measured directly or established as the cause.

warnings: Observed-table mappings override stored rationales and recent-feedback molecule descriptions, especially 66e712388ecd53b9c22c. Candidate IDs contain predictions only, including exact-input matches to observed experiments.

Supplied m177 candidates probe lower ratios; they do not repeat exceptional 20/1, 50 ul or 50/1, 100 ul inputs. Such sampling cannot establish reproducibility. Earlier m207 and m120 depressions also remain unreplicated.

Established m28, m81, m13, m173, m125, m167, m212, m127 and recent m26/m78/m157 contrasts need named remaining questions. Boundary predictions alone do not reopen rejected m80 transition or m68 rebound expectations.

Deduplicate complete molecule/condition tuples unless repetition addresses a named ambiguity. Sample volume and mass are coupled; retain density and loading-solvent identity/volume. Candidate multiplicity does not establish Row prevalence.
V2 minus V1 is elution interval width. Quantile widths and historical premeasurement errors do not establish current error, expected learning gain or retrained Row accuracy.
